images.title: These strange marks are numbers
images.purpose: Shows that the strange wedge marks on an old loose page are numbers written about 4000 years ago.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One loose sheet of pale cream paper, slightly tilted, fills the middle of the frame with three groups of wedge marks on it and a small number under each group.
images.exact_structure: One rectangular sheet of paper (pale cream fill, dark outline, one corner gently curled) tilted about 5 degrees. On it, left to right, three groups of dark wedge marks with clear space between groups: group 1 is exactly one upright wedge (a thin vertical stroke with a triangular head); group 2 is exactly three upright wedges side by side; group 3 is exactly one corner wedge (a sideways V shape opening to the right). Under each group, in teal (#0072B2), its value: 1 under group 1, 3 under group 2, 10 under group 3. Above the sheet, in small grey (#6B7280) text: about 4000 years ago. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Long ago, people wrote numbers with marks very different from our digits.
images.description: Shows that the strange wedge marks on an old loose page are numbers written about 4000 years ago.
images.context: Hook picture for the loose page; Mesopotamian upright wedge is 1 and corner wedge is 10.
images.teaching_notes: Keep it to three groups so the child can decode them; 20, 50, 100 stay an open question.

image_decisions.why: The hook needs one clear picture of the mystery: old marks that turn out to be numbers.
